## Intentional divergences

### TOOL-REFERENCE-ABI — Reference MIPS/SPIM ABI compatibility

- Boundary: Generated stack bytecode, pseudo-assembly, object layout, calling convention, and packages are Cooler-native and are not MIPS/SPIM artifacts.
- Reason: The product is a portable educational compiler lab with an inspectable Go VM, not a replacement for the historical CS143 backend toolchain.
- User consequence: Users cannot link Cooler output with reference runtime objects or execute its pseudo-assembly in SPIM; only normalized source acceptance and observable program behavior are comparable.
- Scope assertion: README-BACKEND and TOOL-BACKEND-ARTIFACTS claims plus artifact-contract tests prevent pseudo-assembly from being represented as reference assembly.

### TOOL-MODULES — Modules and separate compilation

- Boundary: A project is an ordered set of complete class declarations; imports, module declarations, split classes, object files, and separate linking do not exist.
- Reason: Those constructs are language extensions absent from classic COOL and would change parsing, name resolution, and project semantics.
- User consequence: Users must pass all complete source units together and cannot publish or link separately compiled modules.
- Scope assertion: README-PARSER and README-MULTIFILE claims are audited against PAR-PROGRAM-STRUCTURE and TOOL-MULTIFILE, whose fixtures reject incomplete/split declarations and preserve ordered whole-program semantics.
